backlogged.summary: The base-side vacuity limit only applies to `verify.vacuity_timeout_sec` inside `verify()`. `run --resume` state files written before F33 have no `vacuity_timeout_sec`, so they fall back to DEFAULTS through `?? DEFAULTS.verify.vacuity_timeout_sec`. That is correct, but no test covers a resumed snapshot without the key.

A base run that times out is treated as non-vacuous. A criterion whose check hangs on base for reasons unrelated to the feature therefore skips the vacuity guarantee, and only `base_timed_out: true` in the result records this. This follows the contract, but nothing in the verify output or the eval prompt surfaces the flag to a human or the evaluator.

The F33 tests rely on wall-clock timing: 3 s and 10 s vacuity limits, a 5 s head check, and a 3 s pid-liveness wait. They may flake on a heavily loaded host, as B177 and B185 already note for other tests.
Base vacuity runs are never retried alone (B182). With F33 a base timeout caused by contention also counts as non-vacuous. The SPEC §6.3 addition does not mention this interaction.

A base timeout now counts as 'did not pass on base'. A check that really passes on base but takes longer than vacuity_timeout_sec (default 120s, e.g. a slow full test suite) is therefore reported as non-vacuous, and a vacuous criterion can pass. The contract (AC-2) and SPEC §6.3 specify this behaviour. Consider adding a warning line to the verify output when base_timed_out is set, so a reviewer can notice it.

verify.vacuity_timeout_sec accepts any positive number, including very small ones such as 0.001. With such a value every base vacuity run times out, which in effect turns off the vacuity check for all new criteria without any warning. Consider a minimum value, or a doctor or verify warning for values below a few seconds.

Only the timed-out case is distinguished for base runs. A base run that fails because a program is missing is still counted as non-vacuous, with no environment-stop signal. This existing gap is unchanged by F33.

A base run that fails only because of contention with concurrent runs is still never retried alone. F33 adds timeouts as a second way for a base run to count as non-vacuous without a real fail on base.
